unwritten_consumer_rules.rule: Decision must carry decision_id==envelope.decision_id, effect_id==envelope.effect_id, a non-None binding, and binding.grant_id/grant_revision/effective_max_effects equal to envelope values. effective_max_effects binding is not described in docs/execution-boundary.md (steps 2 and 5 only say 'persisted decision identity').

proposal_commitment must equal agent_control_plane.bounded.commitment(proposal.model_dump(mode='json', exclude_none=False)); tenant_id read via getattr default None and must match envelope tenant (issue #95).

Authority Context must expose context['institution']['institution_id'] and ['authority_domain']; in runtime_authority_profile mode the Manifest action's 'authority_context' dict is assumed to have that same {institution_id, authority_domain} shape (context = {'institution': action['authority_context']}). Shape is not specified in any schema in this repo.

After workflow.execute succeeds, records.reconciliations is assumed non-empty (index [-1]); cp_observation may be None and then status is forced to 'unknown'; local result status takes precedence otherwise (line 342), so status 'unknown' can coexist with a non-null CP observation.

Claim must have profile==PROFILE, authorizing_by_possession is False, grant_status=='active', all approval_state/policy_state status 'active', and evidence_state items with required or unknown_behavior=='hold_effect' must be state 'current'. Only the active/current-projection part is in prose (docs/local-authority-effect-profile.md:27-30); authorizing_by_possession, hold_effect and profile equality are not documented anywhere.

Runtime recomputes the claim operation_commitment with its own field list (excludes proposal_commitment and effective_max_effects; tenant_id only if not None) using CP's commitment(); this must match CP's algorithm/field list exactly. Not documented.
21 claim fields must equal the envelope (incl. payload_commitment, requested_permissions tuple equality, float(amount)).

If control_plane_evidence.reconciliation exists: reconciliation.effect_id==effect_id, retry_eligible must be exactly False, a non-empty observation must equal reconciliation.observation and observation_accepted must be True, rejected observation requires observed_state 'unknown'. Only the retry_eligible=false preservation is mentioned as guidance (docs/executor-producer-profile.md:54-56); the equality/accepted rules are not.

CP attempt evidence must be a dict with decision_id, effect_id (and attempt_id when result.attempt_id is not an executor attempt) matching the envelope; 'observation.control_plane_attempt_evidence' legacy key also accepted (line 100).

A destination observation with state 'unknown' is treated as terminal for the attempt (status 'unknown', no commit retried). Implied by OpenShell design, written in docs/openshell-adapter.md:153-157 only for OpenShell.

Executor error strings {effective_grant_changed_at_commit, effective_grant_precondition_required, atomic_authority_capability_unavailable, effective_grant_permissions_insufficient, effective_grant_permissions_unavailable} are mapped to CP DefinitiveDestinationRejection; CP must treat that class as definitive non-effect. Coupling by exact error text; not specified in docs.

unwritten_rules_method: For each candidate rule I grepped docs/*.md, README.md and *.md for the field/value names (hold_effect, authorizing_by_possession, grant_status, effective_max_effects, runtime_authority_profile, authority_context, observation_accepted, retry_eligible, model_dump, exclude_none, proposal_commitment, tenant). No JSON schema files exist in the repo (git ls-files | grep schema: only engine/action_schema.py, an unrelated action validator). Absence from prose was judged by grep, not by reading every workstream document; docs/workstreams/*.md/json not read in full.

route_unknown_findings.route_labels_in_repo: Only 'route A' (PinnedControlPlaneExecutor, CA:165; tests/test_route_a_*.py, CHANGELOG.md:9,14, docs/execution-boundary.md:150) and 'route B' (atomic claim route = AtomicLocalControlPlaneExecutor; tests/test_atomic_post_commit_unresolved.py:5; CHANGELOG.md:18 'atomic claim route') are named. 'Route C' is not defined anywhere in this repo (grep route.?c over code/docs/tests). Closest candidate, treated here as route C: the OpenShell destination (OpenShellRefundDestination) run through route A. Caller should confirm the mapping.

route_A.observation: status 'unknown', attempted True, acknowledged False, newly_executed False; observation = destination.observe_bound(snapshot) result (so state applied|partial|absent|unknown with destination_state), or fallback {effect_id,state:'unknown',destination_state:{}} if that read raises (894-896); error=str(exc); attempt event 'unknown' (897). observed_state = observation['state'].

existing destination state 'unknown' (only a destination like OpenShell returns it) -> status 'unknown', observation=existing (state unknown, destination_state {}), acknowledged True, newly_executed False.
adapter raises TimeoutError when local status is unknown, handing lost-ack handling to the Control Plane workflow.

final route-A result: state = cp_observation.state or 'unknown'; status = local.status (so 'unknown' persists even if CP later accepts an applied/partial observation, line 342); if cp_observation is None status is forced 'unknown' (345-346) and observation=None (347-349) even though acknowledged may be True and the destination may hold an effect (docs/executor-producer-profile.md:31-35). control_plane_evidence carries attempt+reconciliation (337-340). So route A can emit unknown with a null observation, and unknown with a non-null CP observation of any state (producer_contract.py:144-146 refuses to export a non-empty observation unless reconciliation.observation_accepted is True and equal; whether CP ever returns a rejected observation from workflow.execute is not visible in this repo). The local executor's own observation never reaches the result on route A because CA:347-349 always substitutes the CP one.

route_B.observation: status 'unknown', attempted True, acknowledged False, newly_executed False; observation = destination.reconcile_claim() dict {status applied|partial|hold, claim_state, retry_eligible:false, effect_id, operation_digest|reason}; fallback {'status':'unknown','retry_eligible':False,'reason':'reconciliation_unavailable'} (51); observed_state is recovery['status'] only if applied|partial else 'unknown' (71). The observation is a local claim-store reconciliation, not a Control Plane validated EffectObservation, and has no 'state' key. control_plane_evidence={failure_record_id, failure_class:'dispatch_error'} (75-78). failure_records_v1 row reason_code post_commit_observation_unavailable | acknowledgement_unavailable (55-62).

route_C_openshell_destination.where: engine/openshell_environment.py:361-386 commit(): any exception after intent insert -> TimeoutError('sandbox dispatch outcome requires destination observation'); prior unresolved intent raises TimeoutError (370)
route_C_openshell_destination.observation: Caught by LocalDestinationExecutor.execute_snapshot (SE:892) which calls observe_bound again (894) and returns status 'unknown' with that observation.

Validated observation: _validate_observation (297-340) runs on the sandbox result (line 347) and accepts only {effect_id,state,destination_state} with state absent|applied|partial and field-by-field agreement with the snapshot; absent + pending dispatch_intents is rewritten to synthesized {state:'unknown',destination_state:{}} (350-351); non-PermissionError failures return the same synthesized unknown (357-359); PermissionError (validation failure) is re-raised (354-356) and the executor then records 'denied' (SE:841-854) or falls back to unknown at SE:896.

route_unknown_findings.route_C_unknown_with_validated_observati: YES, as code allows. In OpenShellRefundDestination.commit, after a process acknowledgement observe_bound (line 378) can return a _validate_observation-validated state applied|partial; if the acknowledgement's 'duplicate' is not a bool (381-382) the code raises TimeoutError (385-386). execute_snapshot then catches it (SE:892), re-reads observe_bound (894), which returns the validated applied/partial row, and emits status 'unknown' with observed_state applied|partial and observation = that validated row (SE:898-909). Same path with observed state 'absent' (379-380): absent is validated, but pending dispatch_intents rewrites it to 'unknown' on the re-read. Under route A the CP wrapper then replaces observation with the CP observation (CA:341-349). Not executed; read-only inspection.
route_unknown_findings.caveat: 'unknown' status can therefore co-occur with observed_state applied/partial, so an ODES lifecycle consumer cannot infer 'no known effect' from status=='unknown'; see producer_contract.py:153-160 which still requires retained effect rows for executed/reconciled/partial but not for unknown.

notes: Blocker: ExecutionResult.status vocabulary mixes attempt outcome and destination state; 'unknown' appears with observed_state applied/partial (SE:892-909, CA:342) and with observation null (CA:345-349). A decoupled lifecycle contract needs to define status vs observed_state vs observation separately.
